slides.0.title: Getting to Know the Rhône Valley
slides.0.subtitle: Geography, history and the north–south divide
slides.1.title: Where is the Rhône Valley?
slides.1.highlights.0.title: A region shaped by a river
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The valley runs from around Vienne south to around Avignon, roughly 200 km (approximate — sources draw the start and end points differently), heading towards the Mediterranean
slides.1.highlights.1.title: North: steep and narrow
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Northern Rhône means steep slopes, small and terroir-led appellations, mostly on ancient igneous and metamorphic rock
slides.1.highlights.2.title: South: open and rolling
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Southern Rhône is open, gently rolling country with younger, more varied soils, larger appellations and blending at its heart
slides.1.highlights.3.title: A lopsided split in output
slides.1.highlights.3.content: The great majority of output comes from the south (commonly put at 95%+, an approximation); the north is small yet home to many of the most famous wines
slides.1.content: North and south Rhône are often treated as "one river, two regions": learn them separately, then compare.
slides.2.title: From Roman times to Châteauneuf-du-Pape
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Ancient viticulture
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Wine here goes back more than 2,000 years: Greek settlers founded Massalia (Marseille) at the river mouth around 600 BCE, and the Romans later pushed viticulture north up the Rhône, with Vienne an important northern base
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The papacy moves to Avignon
slides.2.highlights.1.content: From 1309 the papacy was based in Avignon (about 1309–1376), and the demands of the pope and his court stimulated vineyards around the city
slides.2.highlights.2.title: The name Châteauneuf-du-Pape
slides.2.highlights.2.content: The name means "the pope's new castle", linked to papal-era building and vineyards here
slides.2.content: Sources differ slightly on dates in this history; the lesson uses the more widely cited versions.
slides.3.title: Forerunner of the AOC system
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Baron Le Roy's contribution
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Baron Le Roy de Boiseaumarié, a Châteauneuf-du-Pape estate owner, drew up appellation rules in the 1920s (commonly given as 1923), inspiring INAO and the AOC system
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Châteauneuf-du-Pape, 1936
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Châteauneuf-du-Pape received its AOC in 1936, among the earliest in France
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Côtes du Rhône, 1937
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Côtes du Rhône AOC was established by decree on 19 November 1937; in the north, Côte-Rôtie and Condrieu gained AOC status in 1940
slides.3.content: The Rhône is one of the birthplaces of France's AOC system, a frequent exam background point.
slides.4.title: The Rhône at a glance (2025 figures)
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Scale
slides.4.highlights.0.content: About 60,000 ha of vineyard and roughly 2.0 million hl (Inter Rhône Key Figures 2025, 2025 harvest; the report's cover shows 63,931 ha and 2,353,260 hl on a different basis, so only approximations are used)
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Red-led
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Exports
slides.4.highlights.2.content: In 2025 about one-third of volume was exported (about two-thirds sold in France); top markets were Belgium, the UK and the USA
slides.4.highlights.3.title: Producers
slides.4.highlights.3.content: About 6,371 production units and 366 trading companies (négociants) in 2025
slides.4.content: Figures shift with year and basis; always cite the year. The quizzes test only the big picture.
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
How is Rhône output broadly split between north and south?
B. The great majority comes from the south
C. The great majority comes from the north
D. All of it comes from the south
The south's large appellations supply the vast majority; the north is small but home to many famous wines.
From 1309 the papacy moved to which city, boosting nearby vineyards?
The papacy sat in Avignon (about 1309–1376), and the name Châteauneuf-du-Pape is tied to this period.
Who drafted rules for Châteauneuf-du-Pape and is seen as a key figure behind France's AOC system?
Baron Le Roy de Boiseaumarié owned a Châteauneuf-du-Pape estate and later helped found INAO.
